what: a real PostgreSQL restore of a fresh, verified backup into an isolated, disposable cluster

target.isolation: a cluster created for this rehearsal on a non-default port with its own superuser and password; production was never written to, and restore_db.py refuses any target outside LOCAL_HOSTS unless --allow-remote is passed

source.snapshot: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction spanning all 45 public tables
source.verifyResult: artifact: 45 of 45 files match the manifest
source.sealedNote: produced locally by tools/cloud_backup.py. The Google upload steps are OFF because GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, BACKUP_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID and BACKUP_SHEET_ID are unset, so this copy exists on this machine only and was never uploaded. The sealed, off-machine copy is recorded in offMachineSealedCopy below.

offMachineSealedCopy.sealedWith: tar | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 200000 -salt -pass env:KEY; key held only in the WORKER_ARTIFACT_KEY Actions secret
offMachineSealedCopy.residualGap: the sealing key is not available in this environment, so today's restore rehearsal ran against the local plaintext artifact rather than by decrypting the sealed one. A sealed-artifact decrypt-then-restore was last exercised on 2026-10-15 (run 38712534137, still unexpired) by an operator who held the key. Closing that specific path needs WORKER_ARTIFACT_KEY access.

schemaPreparation: npx prisma migrate deploy applied all 36 migrations to the empty target, landing on 20261017150000_eventimpact_reindex -- the exact migration the backup was taken at
toolResult: restore: VERIFIED: 44 tables, 1,335,379 rows, content digests equal
theOneDifference: the tool verifies 44 tables and 1,335,379 rows; the manifest counts 45 and 1,335,415. The difference is _prisma_migrations (36 rows), which the restore deliberately does not load because the target was migrated by Prisma and supplies its own history. Every data table matches exactly.

target.dataDirectory: session scratchpad, deleted after the rehearsal
